positions.commentary: The speaker notes that Microsoft has had success by legally or illegally stealing from other companies, citing examples like Word from WordPerfect and Excel from Lotus 1-2-3.
The speaker mentions owning a Ferrari 488 Spider in 2018 which was a joy to own but got rid of it because it was impractical in the hills.

thesis: This episode offers a collection of personal anecdotes and neutral observations rather than a cohesive investment thesis. The speaker discusses his experiences with Microsoft, Burger King, Ferrari, and RAM Trucks, noting their market positions or personal utility without expressing a clear bullish or bearish stance on any of them.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Microsoft has had success by legally or illegally stealing from other companies, citing examples like Word from WordPerfect and Excel from Lotus 1-2-3.
claims.quote: almost everything Microsoft has had a success at, they have either stolen stolen legally or illegally from some other company. They have a very large budget for their research labs, which in several decades has produced almost nothing.

claims.claim: The speaker describes Burger King as having two guys who clone McDonald's locations and do pretty well.
claims.quote: And Burger King has two guys, and they just look at where McDonald's is putting up locations, and then they go and clone it. And those two guys and their dog do pretty well.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions owning a Ferrari 488 Spider in 2018 which was a joy to own but got rid of it because it was impractical in the hills.
claims.quote: So I got my, my 488 Spider Ferrari in 2018, and that was such a joy and fun to own. But when I moved here, because I live in the hills, and it's a very low car, It just wasn't practical. So I got rid of the Ferrari

claims.claim: The speaker says he got a RAM Longhorn truck after moving to Austin and it is his favorite car.
claims.quote: after moving to Austin, I just moved to Austin, I just got a ram longhorn, and it is so awesome. And, you know, I got to know, the owners of Ferrari when I owned the stock, and it's a very deep regret of mine that, so I'm, I'm not a Ferrari kind of guy, but I felt like I made so much money on Ferrari that I should own a Ferrari.
